newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul hunts communist moles after defector tip-off.
newsitem.headline: Seoul hunts communist moles after defector tip-off.

text.p: A hunt is under way for North Korean spies in the South after a tip-off from a top Pyongyang defector, a senior intelligence official said on Thursday.

Hwang Jang-yop has told Seoul investigators that an extensive network of moles regularly sent intelligence reports to North Korean leader Kim Jong-il, according to Eom Ikk-joon, a vice director of Seoul's Agency for National Security Planning.

"Although Mr Hwang Jang-yop had not worked in anti-South intelligence units, he had gathered informaton about their operations while serving as a high-ranking official in the North," Eom told reporters.

The agency had completed debriefing Hwang, the Stalinist North's former top ideologue, who defected to the South Korean embassy in Beijing in February and eventually arrived in Seoul in April via the Philippines.

Hwang had offered names of South Koreans and others he met in Pyongyang and elsewhere before seeking defection, Eom added. But he denied local news reports that Hwang had said more than 50,000 spies operated in the South.
Hwang told reporters on Thursday the moles not only passed on secrets but tried to foment social turmoil in the South.
